coachingPoints: One dribble only — the move's power is its speed; extra dribbles invite the defense back.
Push the ball out in front on the dribble so your body stays behind the defender's reach.
Eyes to the rim on the dribble, not on the ball — the read happens during the bounce.
Practice the exact game rhythm: catch, one hard dribble, stop, shoot — no pauses between phases.
Add it after your catch-and-shoot reps so the two shots share identical footwork.
commonMistakes: Taking two or three dribbles and calling it 'one' — fix: film it; players consistently underestimate their dribble count.
Dribbling into a crowd — fix: the one-dribble is for small gaps; if the lane is closed, pass or relocate.
Stopping off-balance after the dribble — fix: the dribble should travel toward your shooting pocket, not away from your body.
Rising too slowly — fix: the stop-to-shot must be one motion; a hitch at the bottom kills the advantage.
description: One hard dribble to escape the closeout, then rise into the jumper — the essential counter for every shooter.
gameSituations: Attacking a hard closeout — the defender flies at you; one dribble past him creates an open pull-up.
Catching with a defender in your airspace — instead of forcing a contested catch-and-shoot, dribble into space and shoot clean.
Wing isolations — catch on the wing, one dribble toward the middle, rise for the jumper over a smaller defender.

howTo.detail: Catch the ball in your shot-ready stance, but read the closeout: if the defender is sprinting at you, the drive lane or the sidestep is open.
howTo.title: Catch and read the closeout

howTo.detail: Attack his lead foot with one hard, low dribble — past his hip, not into his chest. The dribble should carry you 3–5 feet into open space.
howTo.title: Take one explosive dribble

howTo.detail: Gather as the ball returns and stop with a 1-2 or hop, landing balanced and square. Your momentum should carry upward, not sideways.
howTo.title: Stop on balance

howTo.detail: Rise straight into your jumper the instant your feet set. The release should happen before the recovering defender can contest.
howTo.title: Rise into the shot

howTo.detail: Finish with full mechanics and hold the follow-through. One-dribble pull-ups should look exactly like your set shot.
howTo.title: Finish like a normal jumper

title: One-Dribble Pull-Up
whatIsIt: The one-dribble pull-up is exactly what it sounds like: catch the ball, take one hard dribble, and rise into your jumper. It is the bridge between catch-and-shoot and full shot creation — the simplest way to turn a contested catch into an open shot.
Shooters live on this move. A defender sprinting at you to contest the three has committed his momentum; one dribble sideways or past him, and that momentum becomes your separation.
whyItMatters: Closeouts are the defense's answer to great shooting, and the one-dribble pull-up is the offense's answer to closeouts. A shooter who can only catch and shoot is playable; a shooter who punishes every hard closeout with a dribble into space is unguardable. It is also highly efficient — one dribble means minimal time for help to arrive.
